history.summary: DUPLICATE FLAG: this row is a confirmed duplicate of seq 987 (id bhadrakali-temple-warangal); retained as a separate record per the spec. One of the oldest temples of Telangana, dedicated to Goddess Bhadrakali, on the banks of the Bhadrakali Lake between Hanamkonda and Warangal. As per the writings on the temple wall, the Chalukya king Pulakesi II built the temple around 625 AD to commemorate his victory over the Vengi region of Andhra Desham; the square pillars (distinct from the circular pillars of Kakatiya temples) attest to the Chalukya work, while the stone entrance gateways reflect the Kakatiya style. The Kakatiya kings of the Orugallu (Warangal) empire adopted Bhadrakali as their Kula Devatha; the lake was built by Ganapathi Deva's minister Hari, who also added a road to the temple. The temple fell into disrepair during the long Muslim rule of the region. In 1950 Sri Ganapathi Shastri, a Devi upasaka, with the help of merchants and affluent people of the region, carried out a large-scale renovation - installing a Chandi Yantra in the shrine, writing beejaksharas on the deity's hanging tongue, and transforming the fierce-looking form into a benevolent one. In the 2000s the temple was expanded with the Alaya Shikharam, Maha Mantapam, parikrama and a new Sri Vallabha Ganapathi temple. The idol is the Ekanda Shila trademark single-stone sculpture of the Chalukyas; the inner Antralaya stambam pillar carries a Sanskrit inscription. CSV town 'Warangal' is accurate - the temple lies between Hanamkonda and Warangal on the lake, in Warangal district.

name: Bhadrakali Temple
town_description: Warangal (Orugallu) is the historic Kakatiya capital city in Telangana, now part of the Warangal-Hanamkonda-Kazipet tri-city. The temple stands on a hill on the banks of the Bhadrakali Lake between Hanamkonda and Warangal, surrounded by hills and rock formations, with the lake adding to its serenity.
